meta.title: Abrus Krishna Finance WordPress Development — Case Study | Teknoppy
meta.description: How Teknoppy built abruskrishna.com on WordPress for a KML-registered Kerala gold loan and micro-finance company, with clear service separation and compliance-ready content.

sections.h1Rest: Built for a Regulated Lending Business

paragraphs.text: Abrus Krishna Finance is a Kerala Money-Lenders Act (KML) registered lending institution based in Guruvayoor, offering gold loans, doorstep gold loans, and a range of micro business, personal, home, and consumer goods loans since 2018.

items.title: No dedicated page per loan product
items.text: All eight loan types were likely bundled into one generic loans/services page, making it hard for a borrower to find the specific product they needed.

items.title: Compliance treated as an afterthought
items.text: No dedicated KML Registration & Compliance page or FAQ answers covering branch-visit requirements, foreclosure rules, or data confidentiality — regulatory trust wasn't built into the content.

items.title: Cannibalization risk between related products
items.text: Gold Loan and Doorstep Gold Loan, two closely related products competing for similar search terms, had no deliberate structure keeping them distinct.

items.title: No visible borrower process
items.text: The loan journey — contact/visit, document verification, approval, disbursement — wasn't laid out clearly, leaving first-time borrowers unsure what to expect before applying.

paragraphs.text: Teknoppy's goal was to build a WordPress site that could present eight distinct loan products clearly, keep regulatory trust (KML registration, transparent terms) visible throughout, and avoid the keyword overlap risk that comes with closely related loan products like gold loan and doorstep gold loan sitting on the same domain.

sections.h2: A comprehensive range of services offered by Teknoppy and their outcomes

items.title: Eight loan products, eight distinct pages
items.text: Gold Loan, Gold Loan in Guruvayoor, Doorstep Gold Loan, Business Loan in Guruvayoor, Business & Micro Enterprise Loan, Micro Personal Loan, Micro Home Loan, Micro Finance, and Consumer Goods Loan each have their own dedicated page rather than being bundled into one generic services page.

items.title: Regulatory trust built into the structure
items.text: KML registration, a dedicated KML Registration & Compliance page, and compliance-specific FAQ answers (branch-visit requirements, foreclosure rules, data confidentiality) are all first-class content, not an afterthought.

items.title: Cannibalization-aware page separation
items.text: Gold Loan and Doorstep Gold Loan — two closely related products that could easily compete for the same search terms — are structured as clearly distinct pages targeting different intents, avoiding the internal competition a less careful build would create.

items.title: A four-step process made visible
items.text: Contact/Visit → Document Verification → Approval → Disbursement is laid out clearly on the homepage, setting expectations for a first-time borrower before they apply.

paragraphs.text: Discovery, design, and build details specific to this project — timeline and key decisions — should be pulled from the project intake and added here once confirmed.

sections.h2: Abrus Krishna Finance's Final Outcome After Teknoppy's Work

items.q: What was the main goal of the Abrus Krishna Finance website project?
items.a: To give a KML-registered lending company a WordPress site that presents eight distinct loan products clearly, keeps regulatory trust visible, and avoids keyword competition between closely related loan pages.

items.q: What loan products does Abrus Krishna Finance offer online?
items.a: Gold Loan, Doorstep Gold Loan, Business Loan, Micro Business/Enterprise Loan, Micro Personal Loan, Micro Home Loan, Micro Finance, and Consumer Goods Loan.

items.q: Did the project affect Abrus Krishna Finance's existing rankings?
items.a: The project was scoped to avoid keyword cannibalization — particularly between the Gold Loan and Doorstep Gold Loan pages — and no overlapping targets were introduced.

items.q: What platform was the site built on?
items.a: The site was built on WordPress using Elementor.
